projects.title: FidelityMem — Adaptive Hybrid Memory
projects.description: A recall-constrained hybrid memory layer that controls active context, long-term storage, compression and evidence restoration for LLM agents.
projects.readme_overview: Module Role --- --- window.py Adaptive working window: per-message retention score, boundary triggers (token pressure, topic shift, task completion, inactivity), eviction into extraction. extraction.py Candidate memories with types (semantic / episodic / procedural / relational), entities, numbers, dates, negations, relations. validation.py Stage 1 source & consistency (trust, contradiction, supersede-not-delete, untrusted-instruction guard). Stage 2 relevance & utility (durability score, fact-aware dedupe). compression.py Four-level compression ladder and the fidelity gate : probes built from the raw source must survive, or the level backs off. Stage 3. stores/ Immutable archival store (JSONL-persistable), BM25, dense index with a hermetic hashing embedder, relation graph with relation-following expansion and hub penalty, trie for exact/prefix identifiers. retrieval/ Query classification, per-type plans, RRF fusion + ranking function, relation chaining for multi-hop, sufficiency check and raw-source expansion, token-budgeted context. controller.py Recall-constrained policy search over (compression level, top-k, expansion budget, routes) with tuning/hold-out split, promotion, rejec
verified_features: needs ANTHROPIC API KEY (or ANTHROPIC AUTH TOKEN / ant auth login )

Dispatch: nearest-rider offers with timeouts; the rider accepts or declines. Live rider location for the customer.

Maps, routes and live tracking: the customer searches for a destination by name, sees the pickup, destination and the road between them on a map, and watches the driver's vehicle (a bike, auto, sedan or SUV) move live; the driver sees every offer, and the trip, on a map. projects.readme_overview: Permission-aware, cited semantic search over public health documents. Built stage by stage, with every design decision and measurement logged. Live app: https://health-semantic-search.onrender.com (free tier: it sleeps when idle, so the first load can take a minute; search only, no cited answers, see below) Research write-up: docs/PAPER.md, a workshop-style draft with every number traced to ENGINEERING LOG.md Full app with cited answers: https://huggingface.co/spaces/Vaibhavbansal26/health-semantic-search-app (same React app, reranker and cited answers; free CPU, so answers take 3-6 s) Original Gradio demo: the Space Vaibhavbansal26/health-semantic-search (reranker, no accounts)
projects.architecture: Layer Choice Notes --- --- --- Front end React 18, Vite 5, plain CSS about 52 kB gzipped; served by the API process, no separate host API FastAPI, uvicorn search, accounts, admin; security headers, per-request access mask Accounts and tokens SQLite, scrypt, PyJWT (RS256) one-hour tokens with a jti , sign-out and admin revocation, login rate limit Keyword search bm25s with a Snowball stemmer index built once, loaded memory-mapped Dense search BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 PyTorch in the full engine, ONNX Runtime (fastembed) in the lite one Fusion and routing weighted reciprocal rank fusion, identifier router NDC, CAS and imprint queries go to keyword search only Reranker and answers bge-reranker-base, extractive answers with a refusal threshold full engine only (about 2 GB) Access control boolean mask inside every retriever, mask-keyed cache document, tenant and section rules Corpus, sync Postgres 16 + pgvector, DailyMed, openFDA, ClinicalTrials.gov connectors kill-safe incremental sync, versioned index publishing Evaluation recall@k, MRR, nDCG, paired bootstrap five model-written question sets, tooling for a real-query set Packaging Docker (multi-stage), Render Blueprint ( render.yaml ) image about 700 MB; runs in under 250 MB of RAM CI GitHub Actions pytest on Python 3.11 and 3.13 (PR 15) Two engines share one API. The full engine ( HSS ENGINE=full ) has the reranker and cited answers and needs about 2 GB. The lite engine ( hss.lite , the default) fits 512 MB: chunk text in SQLite, memory-mapped BM25 and float16 vectors, an ONNX query encoder. On 60 questions it returned the same

projects.readme_overview: Heart-risk estimate + personalised next steps from a hybrid content / collaborative recommender.
verified_features: Risk model — predicts a heart-disease risk score from 11 clinical inputs. Candidates (each in one sklearn Pipeline , imputation fitted inside CV folds): logistic regression, gradient boosting and a PyTorch MLP .
Hybrid recommender — ranks 13 lifestyle / screening / clinical interventions:
Content-based: patient needs (lipids, BP, glucose, fitness, metabolic, cardiac work-up) matched to each intervention's target vector.

Collaborative: a PyTorch two-tower model. The patient tower is an MLP on features plus the mean embedding of interventions the patient already liked; the item tower is an id embedding plus content features. It handles cold start (features only) and warm start (liked items).
Hybrid: α·content + (1-α)·collaborative , with α tuned on a validation split. A safety rule always surfaces a cardiology referral at high scores.
Education links from the NIH/NLM MedlinePlus web service (free, no key).
MLflow experiment tracking and model registry, browsable from the app's 🧪 MLflow tab.

projects.title: Natural Disaster Prediction & Management
projects.description: Natural Disaster Prediction & Management  is a Machine Learning project by Vaibhav Bansal built with Python, Flask, Google API,Machine Learning Algorithms, Deep Learning Methods.
projects.readme_overview: Estimates, live data and alerting for earthquakes, tsunamis, floods, hurricanes and storms. Started as a VIT University capstone in 2020 (Flask 1, TensorFlow 1) and rebuilt in 2026 on FastAPI, scikit-learn, HTMX, Tailwind and Leaflet, with live feeds and a Claude-powered assistant. Outputs are statistical estimates and other organisations' live data. They are not operational forecasts or warnings. Earthquakes cannot be predicted: the earthquake page reports a historical hazard rate, and real-time alerts come from the USGS feed, not from a model.
verified_features: Home: A live 3D globe of this week's USGS earthquakes, with module cards
Earthquake: Historical hazard for any place (rate and probability of M 6, 7, 8), the live USGS map, the week's strongest real earthquakes with one-click "Nearby help"
Flood: River level 1, 3 and 6 hours ahead for one gauge, shown next to "no change"
Tsunami, Hurricane, Storm: Small models with their held-out skill shown on the page
Live: GDACS global alerts, a weather outlook for any place, and the real-event alert watcher
Assistant: Plain-language questions answered with live tools and cited guidance (Claude key needed)
Alerts: Hospitals and police near a place or epicentre, then alert your contacts by email or SMS, optionally in other languages
projects.architecture: This is the short map. Detail lives in code-walkthrough.md (backend), frontend.md (browser side), models.md (every model) and statistics.md (generated numbers). A FastAPI application that renders server-side Jinja2 pages, enhanced with HTMX. Models are trained once from the command line and loaded from disk at request time. Nothing trains, downloads or writes files inside a web request.
